title: Adaptive Kernel Mapper and Capacity Scaling Playbook
author: Priya Nair
body:
Summary:

This playbook describes the Adaptive Kernel Mapper (AKM) and associated capacity-scaling procedures used by the Redwood serving runtime to dynamically select execution kernels and right-size GPU capacity for diverse LLM workloads. The AKM is a runtime component that maps model characteristics and live workload signals to a kernel/quantization/placement profile and triggers scale decisions or fallback policies when thresholds are crossed.

Purpose and scope:
- Document how the AKM makes decisions (inputs, scoring, policies).
- Provide concrete configuration examples and CLI commands for ops.
- Prescribe runbook procedures for performance regressions and capacity incidents.
- Link to profiling and benchmarking artifacts used to tune AKM heuristics.

Intended audience:
- Serving runtime engineers (primary)
- SRE and capacity planners
- Model onboarding and perf benchmarking teams

Key concepts (brief):
- Kernel candidate: a specific combination of operator implementation (CUDA/cuBLAS/cutlass), data type/quantization (fp16/int8), and fusion knobs.
- Profile: measured perf/latency/cost numbers for a model + sequence length distribution + batch shape.
- Cost-utility score: composite metric combining tokens/sec (throughput), p95 latency, and estimated cloud cost per token.
- Mapping policy: a set of rules that prefer lower-latency kernels for low-concurrency, and higher-throughput kernels for high-concurrency.

Architecture overview:
1) Telemetry inputs to AKM:
   - Model metadata: architecture family, layer count, head size, weight dtype (fp32/ptq/q4).
   - Serving signals: current concurrent requests per model, average request size, observed prefix cache hit rate.
   - Perf probes: fast microbenchmarks executed in the background on warm workers to validate kernel latency for target sequence length.
   - Historical profiles: offline benchmark results indexed by model hash and quantization profile.

2) Decision pipeline (high-level):
   - Normalize signals -> derive workload fingerprint.
   - Fetch candidate kernels from catalog filtered by model compatibility.
   - Score candidates using cost-utility function.
   - Run safety checks: memory headroom, kernel stability records, mismatch with policy exclusions (e.g., avoid int8 if regression alert exists).
   - Commit selection to local worker and report to central control-plane for observability and rollouts.

Scoring function example (pseudo):
   score = w1 * norm(tokens_per_sec) - w2 * norm(p95_latency) - w3 * norm(cost_per_token)
Weights (w1..w3) are configurable per customer tier (e.g., enterprise might set w2 higher to prioritize latency).

Kernel catalog (recommended fields):
| kernel_id | dtype | impl | ideal_seq_len | mem_delta | notes |
| KERN_CUTLASS_F16 | fp16 | cutlass-v3 | 512 | +0.2GB | good single-stream latencies |
| KERN_INT8_FUSED | int8 | fused-ops-v2 | 1024 | -1.0GB | best throughput at high concurrency |

Configuration file example (YAML):
```yaml
akm:
  scoring_weights:
    tokens_per_sec: 0.5
    p95_latency_ms: 0.35
    cost_per_token: 0.15
  concurrency_thresholds:
    single_stream: 1
    medium: 4
    high: 32
  safety_filters:
    - max_memory_overcommit: 0.85
    - banned_kernels: [KERN_INT8_FUSED] # temporary blocklist if regression detected
```

Operational runbook: when to invoke the AKM incident procedure
1) Alert types that trigger the runbook:
   - p95 latency breach for a model route > SLO for 10 minutes.
   - Sudden drop in tokens/sec per GPU of > 25% over 5 minutes without matching traffic drop.
   - Repeated OOMs on a worker (>= 3 in 12 hours).

2) Immediate triage steps (first-responder, 0–15 mins):
   1. Check service dashboard: model route, worker hostids, recent kernel changes (control-plane audit).
   2. Run quick perf probe against affected worker: akmctl probe --worker <id> --seq 512 --batch 1 --kernel all.
   3. If probe shows kernel regression vs baseline, add kernel to temporary blocklist and restart worker:
      - akmctl block-kernel --kernel KERN_XYZ --reason "p95 regression"
      - systemctl restart redwood-runtime@<worker>
   4. If OOMs present, reduce per-worker concurrency and enable fallback profile: akmctl set-profile --worker <id> --profile conservative

3) Escalation (15–60 mins):
   - Notify capacity-oncall and SRE (pager duty).
   - Spin up dedicated burst capacity pool for the model (if autoscale failed):
     - terraform apply -var "burst_pool_for=model-abc" ... (link to runbook snippet)
   - If root cause appears to be a kernel regression from a recent rollout, initiate rollback of AKM rollout: akmctl rollback --rollout <id>

4) Post-incident (60+ mins):
   - Collect traces: kernel-specific traces, perf probes, flamegraphs.
   - Run A/B microbenchmarks against candidate kernels offline to validate production behavior.
   - Open a regression investigation (link to regression-triage playbook) and add labels and owners.

Profiling and microbenchmarks (how to reproduce locally)
- Use the perf harness to generate representative requests and measure per-kernel latencies.
- Example command to run a microbenchmark on a dev node:
```bash
python perf/harness/run_microbench.py \
  --model /models/llama-70b/ --sequence 1024 --batch 1 \
  --kernels KERN_CUTLASS_F16,KERN_INT8_FUSED --measure p50,p95
```
- Record results into the benchmark catalog JSON and tag with commit/hash.

Benchmarking suite tie-ins:
- The AKM relies on the benchmarking catalog (benchmarks indexed by model fingerprint). When adding a new model or quant profile, the onboarding pipeline must run the benchmark suite at scale and publish profiles. See related_pages for the canonical onboarding docs.

SLOs and operational thresholds (suggested defaults):
- p50 latency target: <= 30ms for single-stream configs; p95 <= 120ms.
- Throughput target: configurable per model; default tokens/sec >= baseline_profile * 0.85.
- Kernel stability: <= 0.5% error/exception rate in a 24-hour window.

Observability (metrics the AKM emits):
- akm.selected_kernel{model,worker} -> kernel_id
- akm.score_breakdown{model,kernel} -> tokens_per_sec, p95_ms, cost_per_token
- akm.probe_status{worker,kernel} -> ok|regression|oom
- akm.rollback_events -> rollout_id, reason, initiated_by

Common troubleshooting scenarios:
1) p95 spike after kernel swap:
   - Rollback kernel selection and re-run probes. Check NVTX traces for unexpected operator fusion costs.
2) Throughput drop under high concurrency:
   - Ensure batching logic is not constrained by small max_batch_size; inspect batching histograms.
3) Memory headroom dangerously low after selecting int8 path on certain models:
   - Verify quantization table match; fall back to fp16 profile for that model.

Controlled rollouts and safety knobs:
- Rollouts are performed by control-plane and are slow by default (10% of workers every 10 minutes).
- Safety rollback triggers:
  - kernel p95 > baseline * 1.4 for 5m
  - error rate spike > 1% for 10m
  - manual abort by oncall

Example rollout command (ops):
```bash
akmctl rollout --kernel KERN_INT8_FUSED --models "llama-13b,redwood-turbo" --rate 10% --monitor p95:120ms
```

Ownership and contacts:
- Component owner: Priya Nair (serving runtime)
- Supporting teams: perf-benchmarks, model-onboarding, eng-sre
- Oncall rotation: runtime-oncall (see eng-sre oncall roster)

Maintenance and tuning cadence:
- Quarterly review of scoring weights and kernel catalog (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4).
- Monthly automated probes running across representative model set to detect silent regressions.

Appendix A — Useful CLI references:
- akmctl probe --worker <id> --seq <n> --batch <b> --kernel <id|all>
- akmctl set-profile --worker <id> --profile {conservative,balanced,aggressive}
- akmctl block-kernel --kernel <id> --reason "<text>"
- akmctl rollout --kernel <id> --models "<csv>" --rate <pct> --monitor "<metric:threshold>"

Appendix B — Example audit log snippet (control-plane):
[2026-02-18T09:12:34Z] rollout: id=rl-20260218-003 kernel=KERN_INT8_FUSED models=[llama-13b] initiated_by=ci-bot status=partial
[2026-02-18T09:18:05Z] probe: worker=w-130 akm.probe_status=regression kernel=KERN_INT8_FUSED p95_ms=162 baseline_p95=98

Appendix C — Quick checklist for model onboarding teams:
1. Run full benchmark suite (seq 128/512/1024, batch 1..16) and publish catalog entries.
2. Attach profiling traces and memory maps to the profile artifact.
3. If quantizing, run stability validation for 72 hours at low load.
4. Provide recommended default profile for AKM.

Notes and future work:
- Planned: add ML-driven scoring function that learns from production regressions to adjust weights automatically.
- Planned: finer-grained per-operator fallbacks to allow mixed-precision within layers.

References:
- See runtime-architecture and kernel scheduler spec for deeper details on placement and preemption semantics.
- Regression triage playbook for root-cause workflow (related_pages).
